summary: Extract infant/child-food heavy-metal limits from six primary-source regulatory documents

limits.product_scope: Infant formula (婴幼儿配方食品; includes infant formula, follow-up formula, toddler formula, and infant formula for special medical purposes — the latter is excluded from the separate FSMP row and governed here)
limits.basis: as-sold powder / solid product; for liquid infant formula the limit is the value divided by 8 (footnote c: liquid infant formula food is converted into its limit according to the ratio of 8:1)

limits.exact_printed_text: food for special dietary use — infant formula c — 0.08 (calculated as solid product). Footnote c: Liquid infant formula food is converted into its limit according to the ratio of 8:1.
limits.document: GB 2762-2022 National Food Safety Standard — Maximum Levels of Contaminants in Foods (English machine translation; values verified against PDF table images)

limits.product_scope: Fruits, vegetables (excluding single-ingredient root vegetables), mixtures (including grain- and meat-based mixtures), yogurts, custards/puddings, and single-ingredient meats — processed/packaged food intended for babies and young children <2 yr (e.g., ready-to-eat purees)
limits.basis: As-sold / as-packaged (ready-to-eat foods such as purees); document does not indicate any reconstitution
limits.table_and_page: Action levels bulleted list, p. 4 (introduced on p. 3); Lead guidance (Jan 2025). Not a numbered table — the numbered Tables 1-3 are survey occurrence data, not action levels.
limits.exact_printed_text: 10 parts per billion (ppb) for fruits, vegetables (excluding single-ingredient root vegetables), mixtures (including grain- and meat-based mixtures), yogurts, custards/puddings, and single-ingredient meats;
limits.document: Two US FDA Closer to Zero guidances for industry: (1) "Action Levels for Lead in Processed Food Intended for Babies and Young Children" (final, January 2025; docket FDA-2022-D-0278) — file us-fda-c2z-lead-baby-food.pdf; (2) "Inorganic Arsenic in Rice Cereals for Infants: Action Level" (final, August 2020; docket FDA-2016-D-1099) — file us-fda-c2z-ias-infant-rice-cereal.pdf. Action levels apply to processed/packaged food represented for babies and young children under two years old. Note: the lead action levels expressly do NOT apply to infant formula or to any beverages/toddler drinks (Lead guidance, footnote 2, p. 3); lead in juices is addressed in a separate draft guidance.

limits.product_scope: Single-ingredient root vegetables (carrots or sweet potatoes, with or without additional ingredients such as water or preservatives) — processed/packaged food intended for babies and young children <2 yr
limits.basis: As-sold / as-packaged (ready-to-eat single-ingredient root vegetable puree); document does not indicate any reconstitution
limits.table_and_page: Action levels bulleted list, p. 4 (introduced on p. 3); Lead guidance (Jan 2025). 'Single-ingredient root vegetables' defined in footnote 4, p. 4.
limits.exact_printed_text: 20 ppb for single-ingredient root vegetables; and
limits.document: Two US FDA Closer to Zero guidances for industry: (1) "Action Levels for Lead in Processed Food Intended for Babies and Young Children" (final, January 2025; docket FDA-2022-D-0278) — file us-fda-c2z-lead-baby-food.pdf; (2) "Inorganic Arsenic in Rice Cereals for Infants: Action Level" (final, August 2020; docket FDA-2016-D-1099) — file us-fda-c2z-ias-infant-rice-cereal.pdf. Action levels apply to processed/packaged food represented for babies and young children under two years old. Note: the lead action levels expressly do NOT apply to infant formula or to any beverages/toddler drinks (Lead guidance, footnote 2, p. 3); lead in juices is addressed in a separate draft guidance.

limits.document: Two US FDA Closer to Zero guidances for industry: (1) "Action Levels for Lead in Processed Food Intended for Babies and Young Children" (final, January 2025; docket FDA-2022-D-0278) — file us-fda-c2z-lead-baby-food.pdf; (2) "Inorganic Arsenic in Rice Cereals for Infants: Action Level" (final, August 2020; docket FDA-2016-D-1099) — file us-fda-c2z-ias-infant-rice-cereal.pdf. Action levels apply to processed/packaged food represented for babies and young children under two years old. Note: the lead action levels expressly do NOT apply to infant formula or to any beverages/toddler drinks (Lead guidance, footnote 2, p. 3); lead in juices is addressed in a separate draft guidance.

limits.document: Codex CXS 193 — General Standard for Contaminants and Toxins in Food and Feed, Schedule I (Maximum and Guideline Levels for Contaminants and Toxins in Foods), Heavy Metals section. VERSION CAVEAT: although the file is named 'Codex_CXS193_2023.pdf', every page header reads 'CODEX STAN 193-1995' and the page-1 footer reads 'Adopted 1995; Revised 1997, 2006, 2008, 2009; Amended 2009'. This is the 2009-amended edition, NOT the 2023 edition. The infant/child-food entries present in the current (2023-amended) edition are therefore ABSENT here — there are NO MLs for inorganic arsenic in polished/husked rice, and NO dedicated MLs for cereal-based foods for infants and young children, ready-to-eat meals for infants and young children, food for special medical purposes for infants, or follow-up formula. The heavy-metal tables carry a 'Level mg/kg' column (values below converted to µg/kg). The ONLY infant-specific ML printed in this edition is Lead in infant formula (0.02 mg/kg, ready to use, Lead table, p.35). No cadmium, arsenic (total or inorganic), total mercury, or methylmercury ML is assigned to any infant/child food. Basis is indicated in the Notes/Remarks column (e.g. 'Ready to use', 'Ready to drink'), not in a dedicated basis column. The two tin entries below are general canned-food/canned-beverage MLs (suffix 'C' = 'in canned products only') that would apply to a canned infant food or canned infant drink; they are not infant-specific.
